subjects.name: Introduction to Philosophy of the Human Person

competencies.title: Distinguish opinion from truth
competencies.notes: Analyze statements and identify if they are facts or opinions.

questions.question: Which of the following best defines a 'truth' in philosophy?
options: A personal feeling about a certain situation.
A statement that is supported by factual evidence and can be verified.
An idea that is popular among a large group of people.
A suggestion that might be true in the future.
questions.rationale: Truth is characterized by its verifiability and grounding in objective reality, as opposed to subjective opinion.

questions.question: What is the primary characteristic of an 'opinion'?
options: It is universally accepted by all scientists.
It is based on objective observation.
It reflects personal beliefs, feelings, or interpretations.
It remains the same regardless of who says it.
questions.rationale: Opinions are subjective expressions of an individual's perspective and do not necessarily represent objective facts.

questions.question: Which of these is considered a 'fact'?
options: The Philippines is an archipelago.
Adobo is the most delicious dish in the world.
Learning philosophy is boring.
Summer is the best season of the year.
questions.rationale: The statement about the Philippines is a geographical fact that can be verified through maps and data.

questions.question: Why is the statement 'Blue is the prettiest color' classified as an opinion?
options: Because it is supported by color theory.
Because it is a personal preference that cannot be proven true or false for everyone.
Because it can be measured using scientific instruments.
Because it is a rule in art schools.
questions.rationale: Aesthetic preferences are subjective and vary from person to person, making them opinions rather than objective truths.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is a fact?
options: It is a hot day today.
The sun rises in the east.
English is a difficult language to learn.
Chocolate ice cream is better than vanilla.
questions.rationale: The rotation of the Earth resulting in the sun rising in the east is a scientifically verifiable natural phenomenon.

questions.question: If someone says, 'This coffee tastes bitter,' how should we categorize this statement?
options: As a truth, because the person said it.
As an opinion, because taste is subjective to the individual's sensory experience.
As a fact, because coffee contains caffeine.
As a lie, because some people like bitter coffee.
questions.rationale: Sensory experiences like taste are personal perceptions and do not constitute objective truth for everyone.

questions.question: Identify which of the following is an example of an opinion.
options: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
The human heart pumps blood throughout the body.
Playing video games is a waste of time.
Humans require oxygen to survive.
questions.rationale: The utility or value of a hobby is a matter of personal judgment and values, not a verifiable fact.

questions.question: Analyze the following statements and identify the factual one:
options: Math is the most important subject in school.
The Earth revolves around the Sun.
Students are happier when they have shorter classes.
Online shopping is more convenient than going to the mall.
questions.rationale: The heliocentric model of the solar system is an established scientific fact.

questions.question: How can you distinguish a fact from an opinion when reading a news article?
options: By counting how many adjectives the author uses.
By checking if the claim can be proven with evidence or data.
By believing whatever the headline says.
By seeing how many people commented on the article.
questions.rationale: Fact-checking requires looking for evidence and objective data rather than relying on emotional language or popularity.

questions.question: Evaluate the following statement: 'Honesty is the best policy.' Is this a fact or an opinion?
options: It is a fact because everyone knows it.
It is an opinion because it expresses a moral value or guideline for behavior, not a scientific certainty.
It is a fact because it is written in books.
It is neither; it is a mathematical equation.
questions.rationale: Moral judgments and philosophical guidelines for living are based on values, which are subjective opinions rather than empirical facts.

questions.question: Which of the following best defines a statement of truth?
options: A personal belief that cannot be proven.
A claim that is supported by objective evidence and reality.
A subjective preference based on individual feelings.
A guess about the future that may or may not happen.
questions.rationale: Truth is characterized by its correspondence to objective reality and empirical evidence, whereas the other options describe opinions or conjectures.

questions.question: What is the primary characteristic of an opinion?
options: It is universally accepted by all people.
It can be verified through scientific experimentation.
It is a subjective belief that lacks definitive proof.
It is a factual account of historical events.
questions.rationale: Opinions are inherently subjective; they represent individual perspectives or beliefs rather than objectively verifiable facts.

questions.question: Why is the statement 'The weather is uncomfortable today' classified as an opinion?
options: Because it is a scientific observation about humidity.
Because it relies on the speaker's personal feeling rather than a universal standard.
Because it is a historical fact that cannot be changed.
Because it provides data that can be measured by a thermometer.
questions.rationale: Comfort is subjective; what one person finds uncomfortable, another might find pleasant. It lacks a universal standard of measurement.

questions.question: Which of the following statements serves as a clear example of a fact?
options: Water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius at sea level.
Vanilla is the best flavor of ice cream.
Math is the most difficult subject to study.
The government should lower taxes for everyone.
questions.rationale: The freezing point of water is a constant, verifiable, and empirical reality, making it a factual statement.

questions.question: A student claims, 'The school cafeteria serves the best pizza.' How should this be categorized?
options: As a truth, because the student has tasted it.
As an opinion, because 'best' is a value judgment that varies by taste.
As a fact, because the school provides the pizza.
As an error, because pizza quality is non-existent.
questions.rationale: Value-laden words like 'best' indicate personal preference rather than objective truth, categorizing the statement as an opinion.

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios demonstrates the application of distinguishing truth from opinion?
options: Accepting everything a politician says as truth.
Ignoring all opinions and focusing only on reading books.
Validating a claim by checking if it is supported by empirical evidence or consensus.
Believing that all opinions are equally valid regardless of evidence.
questions.rationale: Distinguishing truth involves the practical step of seeking verification and evidence to validate a claim.

questions.question: How can you distinguish a factual statement from an opinion in a news report?
options: Facts use emotional language, while opinions use neutral language.
Facts are verifiable through multiple reliable sources, while opinions reflect the author's bias.
Facts are always written by older people, while opinions are written by younger people.
Facts are always longer than opinions.
questions.rationale: Verification through evidence and the absence of subjective bias are the core analytical tools used to separate facts from opinions.

questions.question: Analyze the following statements and identify which one is a factual claim.
options: The Philippines is an archipelago.
Filipino people are the most hospitable in the world.
It is wrong to criticize government policies.
Living in the province is better than living in the city.
questions.rationale: The geographical status of the Philippines is a verifiable, objective reality, whereas the other options are subjective values or cultural interpretations.

questions.question: Why is it important to evaluate whether a statement is an opinion or a truth before accepting it as 'fact'?
options: To ensure that we only agree with people we like.
To minimize the risk of being misled by misinformation or subjective biases.
To make sure we can win every argument we have with others.
To prioritize our own opinions over everyone else's.
questions.rationale: The critical evaluation of claims is necessary for intellectual integrity and to ensure one's knowledge base is grounded in reality.

questions.question: Evaluate the following argument: 'The movie was boring because it lasted three hours.' Is this a statement of truth?
options: Yes, because the duration of the movie is a factual, measurable, and verifiable truth.
No, because the judgment of 'boring' is a subjective opinion, even if it is linked to a fact.
Yes, because movie duration is a universally accepted standard for quality.
No, because movies cannot be measured by time.
questions.rationale: While the duration (3 hours) is a fact, the conclusion (it is boring) is an interpretation. Thus, the statement as a whole is an opinion based on a personal response to a fact.

competencies.title: Realize that the methods of philosophy lead to  wisdom and truth
competencies.notes: Explore branches like Epistemology and methods like Socratic inquiry.

questions.question: Which branch of philosophy is primarily concerned with the study of knowledge and how we distinguish truth from belief?
options: Ethics
Epistemology
Metaphysics
Aesthetics
questions.rationale: Epistemology is defined as the theory of knowledge, specifically dealing with the nature and scope of knowledge and truth.

questions.question: In the Socratic method, what is the primary goal of asking probing questions to another person?
options: To confuse the listener
To win an argument
To uncover deeper truth and clarify ideas
To prove the teacher is more intelligent
questions.rationale: The Socratic method uses dialectic inquiry to expose contradictions in thought and arrive at a more refined understanding.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'an unexamined life is a life not worth living' imply about the search for wisdom?
options: People should avoid thinking too much to remain happy.
Living without reflecting on one's values and truth hinders true human potential.
One must be a professional philosopher to have a good life.
Examination of life is only necessary when one faces a major crisis.
questions.rationale: Socrates suggests that reflection and questioning are essential to the human experience and the pursuit of wisdom.

questions.question: In Plato's Allegory of the Cave, what do the 'shadows' on the wall represent to the prisoners?
options: The ultimate truth of the universe
The shadows of their own bodies
Illusions and superficial appearances of reality
The light of the sun
questions.rationale: Plato used the cave allegory to illustrate how society often confuses sensory perceptions (shadows) with actual truth.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes Rene Descartes' method of 'Cartesian doubt'?
options: Accepting everything taught by authorities without question.
Rejecting any belief that can be doubted to find a foundation of absolute certainty.
Forgetting all past knowledge to live a life of ignorance.
Trusting only what one's eyes see clearly.
questions.rationale: Descartes believed that by doubting everything uncertain, one could arrive at an indubitable truth (the Cogito).

questions.question: Socrates' 'Three Sieves' test requires that before we speak, our words must pass through filters of truth, goodness, and usefulness. If a piece of information is true but not good or useful, what should one do?
options: Share it because it is true.
Refrain from sharing it.
Ask someone else to share it.
Only share it if it makes the listener angry.
questions.rationale: The Three Sieves suggests that wisdom involves discernment; if information is not helpful or kind, it fails the test of wisdom even if true.

questions.question: How does Descartes' method of doubt function as a tool for a student searching for truth today?
options: It encourages students to ignore their teachers.
It helps students critically evaluate information before accepting it as fact.
It teaches students that nothing can ever be truly known.
It forces students to memorize philosophical definitions.
questions.rationale: Applying Cartesian doubt means not accepting claims blindly, which is a practical skill for modern information literacy.

questions.question: Why does Plato suggest that the prisoner who escapes the cave and sees the sun has a duty to return?
options: To show off his new knowledge.
Because he is forced by his captors.
To enlighten others about the true nature of reality.
Because he finds the outside world too lonely.
questions.rationale: The allegory highlights the philosopher's responsibility to share the truth discovered through reasoning with the rest of society.

questions.question: Which statement best connects the methods of philosophy to the attainment of wisdom?
options: Philosophy relies on luck to find the truth.
The rigorous questioning in philosophy transforms mere opinion into examined knowledge.
Philosophy is just about memorizing the theories of famous men.
Truth is discovered by following the majority opinion in society.
questions.rationale: Philosophy uses logical processes to move from subjective opinion to objective, reasoned understanding (wisdom).

questions.question: Evaluate the following: Why is a person who refuses to question their own beliefs unlikely to reach the 'truth' according to the Socratic tradition?
options: Because truth is found by listening to the loudest person in the room.
Because unexamined beliefs are often based on untested assumptions and biases.
Because questioning is only for students, not for adults.
Because truth is a secret that only ancient philosophers possessed.
questions.rationale: Socratic tradition posits that truth requires active inquiry; avoiding self-reflection leaves one trapped in potential falsehoods or cultural biases.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the Socratic method of seeking truth?
options: Memorizing established dogmas to avoid error
Engaging in dialogue through questioning to reach clarity
Using mathematical proofs to verify sensory perception
Accepting the traditions of the elders without question
questions.rationale: The Socratic method is fundamentally defined by the use of critical questioning to challenge assumptions and arrive at truth, which is a foundational concept in the study of philosophy.

questions.question: What is the primary function of epistemology in the pursuit of wisdom?
options: To study the nature of moral actions
To explore the nature of beauty and art
To examine the nature, origin, and limits of human knowledge
To provide a framework for political governance
questions.rationale: Epistemology is the branch of philosophy concerned with how we know what we know, making it essential for the systematic pursuit of truth.

questions.question: In Plato’s 'Allegory of the Cave', what do the shadows on the wall represent?
options: The ultimate truth of the cosmos
The subjective and often flawed human perception of reality
The divine wisdom granted to the enlightened
The physical objects we touch in our daily lives
questions.rationale: The shadows represent the illusions or mere appearances that people mistake for reality, illustrating the difference between sensory perception and true knowledge.

questions.question: Why did Socrates claim that 'an unexamined life is a life not worth living'?
options: Because intellectual activity is the only path to physical survival
Because humans are defined strictly by their social status
Because reflection is necessary to fulfill one's potential as a rational being
Because unexamined lives inevitably lead to political success
questions.rationale: Socrates emphasized that humans have a duty to critically reflect on their values and beliefs to live a meaningful, virtuous, and truly human life.

questions.question: What does Socrates suggest through his 'Three Sieves' test?
options: To accept information only from those in positions of power
To filter communication through truth, goodness, and necessity before speaking
To prioritize personal opinion over communal agreement
To avoid all speech to prevent conflict
questions.rationale: The Three Sieves act as a pedagogical tool to demonstrate how critical filtering and wisdom lead to more truthful and ethical communication.

questions.question: How does Rene Descartes’ method of 'Cartesian Doubt' function as a tool for finding truth?
options: By accepting the authority of established traditions
By systematically rejecting any belief that can be doubted to reach a foundational certainty
By ignoring all sensory data to focus only on emotions
By trusting all initial perceptions as inherently correct
questions.rationale: Descartes used methodological skepticism to clear away false beliefs, seeking an indubitable foundation for knowledge.

questions.question: When an individual encounters a rumor, how might they apply the 'Three Sieves' of Socrates to demonstrate wisdom?
options: Share the information quickly to ensure everyone is warned
Ask if the information is true, good, and useful before passing it on
Ignore the rumor entirely and focus only on scientific facts
Believe the rumor because it is popular and widely shared
questions.rationale: The application of the three sieves requires the individual to actively evaluate information for truth, goodness, and utility, promoting wisdom in daily interaction.

questions.question: How does the 'Allegory of the Cave' relate to the contemporary problem of 'fake news' or misinformation?
options: It encourages us to ignore all media because it is all false
It suggests that society is often content with comfortable illusions rather than seeking the labor of uncovering the truth
It proves that the government is the only source of objective reality
It implies that sensory reality is the only thing that matters
questions.rationale: The allegory highlights the human tendency to mistake manufactured or superficial narratives (the shadows) for reality, reflecting the modern challenge of distinguishing misinformation from truth.

questions.question: What is the primary philosophical connection between Descartes' doubt and the Socratic method?
options: Both encourage the blind acceptance of traditional authorities
Both rely on the active, critical questioning of assumptions to achieve intellectual clarity
Both argue that truth is impossible to attain for human beings
Both prioritize empirical observation over logical reasoning
questions.rationale: Both methods require the practitioner to dismantle preconceived notions, illustrating that wisdom is not inherent but is the result of a rigorous, critical process.

questions.question: To what extent is the 'examined life' a prerequisite for the attainment of truth and wisdom?
options: The examined life is unnecessary because truth is biologically inherited
The examined life is a burden that prevents people from attaining happiness
The examined life is fundamental, as it allows one to discern reality from mere opinion through self-reflection and inquiry
The examined life is only for philosophers and irrelevant to the general public
questions.rationale: Evaluating the examined life shows that wisdom is not passive; it requires the intellectual rigor to identify personal biases and cognitive traps, thereby validating the competency that philosophy leads to truth.

competencies.title: Evaluate truth from opinions in different situations using the methods of philosophizing
competencies.notes: Identify logical fallacies and distinguish subjective opinions from objective facts.

questions.question: Which of the following refers to a statement that is based on personal beliefs, feelings, or preferences rather than objective evidence?
options: Fact
Opinion
Truth
Evidence
questions.rationale: An opinion is defined by its subjective nature, representing personal perspective rather than established fact.

questions.question: What is the primary characteristic of a 'Fact' in the context of philosophy?
options: It is always supported by someone's feelings.
It can be verified as true or false through objective evidence.
It is a belief held by a large group of people.
It is something that can never be proven wrong.
questions.rationale: Facts are distinguished from opinions by their verifiable, objective nature.

questions.question: Which of these statements is a clear example of an opinion?
options: The Earth revolves around the Sun.
Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
Vanilla ice cream is the best flavor for everyone.
Humans require oxygen to survive.
questions.rationale: Preferences like 'best flavor' are subjective and cannot be proven as universal truths.

questions.question: What does it mean to 'evaluate truth' from opinions in a conversation?
options: To accept everything a person says as truth.
To ignore what the other person is saying.
To determine if a statement is based on verifiable facts or personal biases.
To change the topic to something more agreeable.
questions.rationale: Evaluating truth involves discerning the source and validity of information presented in communication.

questions.question: Which fallacy occurs when someone attacks the person making an argument rather than addressing the argument itself?
options: Ad Hominem
Appeal to Authority
False Dilemma
Bandwagon
questions.rationale: Ad Hominem is a logical fallacy where the character of the opponent is attacked to invalidate their argument.

questions.question: If someone says, 'Everyone in school is wearing these sneakers, so they must be the best shoes to buy,' which fallacy are they using?
options: Ad Hominem
Bandwagon
Appeal to Pity
Equivocation
questions.rationale: The Bandwagon fallacy relies on the idea that something is correct because it is popular.

questions.question: Identify the logical flaw in the statement: 'You should believe my business plan is perfect because I am a very successful person.'
options: False Cause
Appeal to Authority
Hasty Generalization
Circular Reasoning
questions.rationale: This is an appeal to authority (specifically, a questionable one) as the speaker uses their status to justify the quality of their plan.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common method to identify a logical fallacy in a statement?
options: Checking if the conclusion follows logically from the premises provided.
Seeing if the speaker is using loud or aggressive language.
Agreeing with the speaker to maintain social harmony.
Determining if the speaker is a popular public figure.
questions.rationale: Validating an argument requires checking the internal logic and the connection between premises and conclusion.

questions.question: How would you classify the statement, 'If we allow students to use cellphones, eventually no one will study and the school will fail'?
options: Valid argument
Slippery Slope fallacy
Fact-based opinion
Logical deduction
questions.rationale: The Slippery Slope fallacy assumes that a small first step will lead to a chain of related (typically negative) events without sufficient evidence.

questions.question: When evaluating a heated discussion, which action best demonstrates the ability to distinguish truth from opinion?
options: Categorizing claims as either verifiable facts or subjective preferences.
Accepting the opinion of the person who speaks the loudest.
Refusing to participate in the conversation entirely.
Believing only the opinions that align with your own.
questions.rationale: The core of evaluating truth lies in the ability to separate objective, evidence-based claims from subjective, personal viewpoints.

questions.question: Which of the following refers to a statement that expresses a personal belief or judgment that is not necessarily based on objective evidence?
options: Fact
Opinion
Argument
Truth
questions.rationale: An opinion is a subjective belief or judgment, whereas a fact is an objective reality that can be verified.

questions.question: Which logical fallacy occurs when an individual attacks the character of the person making an argument rather than addressing the argument itself?
options: Ad Hominem
Appeal to Authority
Slippery Slope
False Dilemma
questions.rationale: Ad Hominem is a fallacy where the opponent's character is attacked to discredit their argument.

questions.question: What is the primary distinction between a 'truth' and an 'opinion' in the context of philosophy?
options: Truth is based on personal feelings, while opinions are based on scientific data.
Truth is verifiable and universally accepted, while opinion is subjective and individual.
Opinions are always false, while truths are always absolute.
There is no real difference, as all truths are based on perspective.
questions.rationale: Philosophy distinguishes truth as that which aligns with reality or evidence, while opinion remains in the realm of subjective interpretation.

questions.question: Which of the following statements represents a 'False Dilemma' fallacy?
options: If you do not support this policy, you must be an enemy of progress.
Most people agree that this is the best way to handle the problem.
The doctor has many years of experience, so his medical advice must be correct.
I believe that the sunset is the most beautiful time of day.
questions.rationale: A False Dilemma presents only two extreme options, ignoring middle-ground possibilities.

questions.question: In a debate, your opponent claims, 'Everyone is buying this new gadget, so it must be the best one on the market.' Which fallacy is being committed?
options: Bandwagon Fallacy
Appeal to Ignorance
Hasty Generalization
Post Hoc Ergo Propter Hoc
questions.rationale: The Bandwagon fallacy assumes that because many people do or believe something, it must be correct or valid.

questions.question: How would you identify if a person is expressing an opinion rather than stating a fact during a conversation?
options: If the statement uses emotional language or subjective qualifiers like 'best,' 'worst,' or 'should'.
If the statement cites a source from a government institution.
If the statement can be measured using a ruler or a clock.
If the statement is spoken by a teacher or an expert in the field.
questions.rationale: Subjective language and value judgments are key indicators that a statement is an opinion rather than an objective fact.

questions.question: Analyze the following statement: 'My neighbor is a terrible person because he forgot to return my lawnmower; therefore, he cannot be trusted to look after our community park.' What is the logical flaw here?
options: It uses an Appeal to Authority to judge the neighbor.
It makes a Hasty Generalization based on a single, unrelated incident.
It creates a False Dilemma regarding the neighbor's character.
It correctly identifies the causal relationship between lawnmowers and park management.
questions.rationale: The argument makes a sweeping conclusion about the person's character based on a single event, which is a Hasty Generalization.

questions.question: Which of the following arguments contains a 'Slippery Slope' fallacy?
options: If we allow students to use tablets in class, they will eventually stop writing entirely, lose the ability to think, and society will collapse.
If we implement this new testing policy, we need to monitor the results for at least one semester.
Either we increase the budget for education, or the country will fall behind globally.
It is wrong to judge people based on their physical appearance.
questions.rationale: A Slippery Slope assumes that a small first step will lead to a chain of related (and typically negative) events.

questions.question: A politician argues that a proposed law should be rejected simply because it was drafted by a rival party. How can this be evaluated philosophically?
options: The argument is valid because party loyalty is the most important factor in legislation.
The argument is an Ad Hominem fallacy because it focuses on the source rather than the merits of the law.
The argument is sound because rival parties rarely produce effective legislation.
The argument is a factual statement because it acknowledges the origin of the document.
questions.rationale: Evaluating the source rather than the content of the proposal constitutes a logical fallacy, specifically Ad Hominem.

questions.question: Assess the validity of the following claim: 'Since there is no scientific proof that ghosts exist, they must not exist at all.' What is the primary issue in this evaluation?
options: It is a sound argument because it relies on the lack of scientific evidence.
It is a fallacy of 'Appeal to Ignorance' because it assumes absence of evidence is evidence of absence.
It is an example of 'Bandwagon' thinking because most scientists agree.
It is a circular argument because it relies on the definition of a ghost.
questions.rationale: The Appeal to Ignorance occurs when one claims that a proposition is true or false simply because it has not yet been proven otherwise.

subjects.name: Pag-aaral ng Kasaysayan at Lipunang Filipino

competencies.title: Naiuugnay ang mga kultura at kamalayang pangkasaysayan sa sariling konteksto at karanasan
competencies.notes: Focus on Ilaya vs Ilawod, Bahandi, and Sandugo.

questions.question: Ano ang pangunahing kahulugan ng terminong 'Ilaya' sa konteksto ng sinaunang pamayanang Filipino?
options: Dakong ibaba o baybaying dagat
Dakong itaas o kabundukan
Gitnang bahagi ng kapatagan
Pook na malapit sa bukana ng ilog
questions.rationale: Tinutukoy ng 'Ilaya' ang mataas na bahagi o kabundukan, batay sa mga batayang kaalaman sa modyul.

questions.question: Ano ang tawag sa sistema ng pautang o 'honor system' kung saan iniiwan ang kalakal at babayaran na lamang sa susunod na pagkikita?
options: Sandugo
Bahandi
Binatuan
Barter
questions.rationale: Ang 'Binatuan system' ay ang sistema ng tiwala sa palitan ng kalakal sa pagitan ng Ilaya at Ilawod.

questions.question: Alin sa mga sumusunod ang itinuturing na 'bahandi' sa lipunang sinaunang Filipino?
options: Mga produktong agrikultural tulad ng palay
Mga kagamitang yari sa kahoy at dagta
Mga simbolo ng yaman tulad ng porselana, tanso, at gong
Mga isdang huli mula sa dagat
questions.rationale: Ang bahandi ay tumutukoy sa mga bagay na sumisimbolo ng yaman at kapangyarihan gaya ng porselana at tanso.

questions.question: Ano ang pangunahing dahilan kung bakit kinakailangan ng mga taga-Ilawod ang mga produkto mula sa Ilaya?
options: Kailangan nila ng dagta at pagkit para sa teknolohiya at kalakalan
Kailangan nila ng mga gintong alahas para sa ritwal
Kailangan nila ng mga balangay para sa paglalakbay
Kailangan nila ng mga lupang matataba para sa pangingisda
questions.rationale: Ang ugnayan ay nakabase sa pangangailangan: kailangan ng Ilawod ang yamang gubat (dagta, pagkit) mula sa Ilaya.

questions.question: Paano nagsisilbing sentro ng ugnayan ang mga ilog sa sinaunang kalakalan?
options: Ito ang nagsisilbing hangganan ng mga teritoryo ng Ilaya at Ilawod
Ito ang pangunahing daanan ng kalakalan at lokasyon ng mga tabuan
Dito ginaganap ang mga seremonya ng kasal sa pagitan ng mga tribo
Ito ang pangunahing imbakan ng lahat ng bahandi
questions.rationale: Ang mga ilog ang nagsisilbing daluyan ng kalakal at lugar kung saan nagtatagpo (tabuan) ang mga grupo.

questions.question: Bakit itinuturing na kritikal ang katapatan sa sistemang binatuan?
options: Dahil walang batas na nagpaparusa sa magnanakaw
Dahil ang pagbawi ng tiwala ay may kaakibat na kahihiyan at parusa
Dahil mas madaling magpalit ng produkto kung magkaibigan
Dahil ito ang tanging paraan para maging pinuno
questions.rationale: Ang kredibilidad ay nakasalalay sa pagtupad sa pangako; ang paglabag ay nagdudulot ng kahihiyan.

questions.question: Alin sa mga sumusunod ang nagpapakita ng ugnayan ng kabuhayan ng Ilaya at Ilawod sa kasalukuyang panahon?
options: Ang pag-aangkat ng isda mula sa dagat patungo sa mga pamilihan sa kabundukan
Ang pagtatayo ng mga pabrika sa mga bundok
Ang pagbabawal sa kalakalan sa pagitan ng lungsod at kanayunan
Ang paggamit ng mga modernong sasakyan sa halip na ilog
questions.rationale: Ang pangangailangan ng bundok sa dagat (isda/asin) at kabundukan (gulay/kahoy) ay buhay na konsepto sa ating ekonomiya.

questions.question: Kung ikaw ay isang pinuno ng pamayanan, bakit mo pipiliing magsagawa ng Sandugo sa ibang grupo?
options: Upang ipakita na mas malakas ang aking hukbo
Upang pagtibayin ang alyansa at siguraduhin ang kapayapaan
Upang makakuha ng libreng porselana at tanso
Upang kontrolin ang kalakalan ng pangingisda
questions.rationale: Ang Sandugo ay estratehikong paraan upang magkaroon ng alyansa at mapanatili ang kapayapaan.

questions.question: Paano mo maiuugnay ang konsepto ng 'bahandi' sa kasalukuyang pagpapahalaga natin sa mga materyal na bagay?
options: Ginagamit natin ang mga ito pangunahing pagkain
Itinuturing natin itong simbolo ng katayuan sa lipunan at yaman
Hindi na mahalaga ang mga materyal na bagay sa modernong panahon
Ang mga ito ay ginagamit lamang bilang dekorasyon sa bahay
questions.rationale: Tulad ng bahandi, ang mga bagay na materyal ay madalas gamitin bilang batayan ng katayuan sa lipunan.

questions.question: Batay sa ugnayang Ilaya at Ilawod, ano ang implikasyon ng pagkakaiba ng kanilang kabuhayan sa kanilang pag-unlad?
options: Nagdulot ito ng hindi pagkakaunawaan at digmaan
Naging daan ito upang maging independyente ang bawat isa
Nagbunsod ito ng pagtutulungan at interdependence upang matugunan ang kanilang pangangailangan
Nagdulot ito ng paghina ng kanilang teknolohiya dahil sa pag-asa sa iba
questions.rationale: Ang pagkakaiba ng resources (specialization) ay nagtulak sa kanila na makipagpalitan para sa kanilang mga kakulangan.

questions.question: Ano ang papel ng 'tiwala' sa pagpapanatili ng sistema ng kalakalan sa pagitan ng magkakaibang pamayanan?
options: Ito ang nagbibigay ng pagkakataon na manloko sa kapwa
Ito ang pundasyon na nagbibigay-daan sa pangmatagalang ugnayan at seguridad
Ito ay opsysonal lamang sa mga maliliit na kalakalan
Ito ay hadlang sa mabilis na pagyaman ng mga negosyante
questions.rationale: Ang tiwala ay kritikal dahil wala silang nakasulat na kontrata gaya ng sa modernong panahon.

questions.question: Suriin ang ugnayan ng Ilaya at Ilawod: Paano nakaapekto ang heograpiya sa kanilang kultura?
options: Ang heograpiya ay nagtakda ng kanilang hanapbuhay at mga produktong ipinagpapalitan
Ang heograpiya ay walang kinalaman sa kanilang pag-unlad
Pinilit ng heograpiya ang mga taga-Ilaya na tumira sa dagat
Naging hadlang ang bundok at dagat upang sila ay mag-usap
questions.rationale: Ang pisikal na lokasyon (bundok vs. dagat) ay direktang humubog sa kanilang kabuhayan.

questions.question: Bakit maituturing na isang matalinong stratehiya ang sistemang 'Sandugo' at pag-aasawahan sa pagitan ng mga pamayanan?
options: Dahil ito ay nakakabawas sa gastos ng pagkain
Dahil ito ay nag-aalis ng pangangailangan sa militar
Dahil pinapatibay nito ang alyansa na nagreresulta sa katatagan ng kalakalan at seguridad
Dahil ito ay nagbibigay ng karapatan sa mga pinuno na sakupin ang ibang lupa
questions.rationale: Ang mga seremonya ay social technologies upang mapanatili ang kooperasyon kaysa kompetisyon.

questions.question: Gaano kahalaga ang konsepto ng 'Ilaya' at 'Ilawod' sa pag-unawa sa ating kasaysayan bago ang kolonyalismo?
options: Hindi ito mahalaga dahil wala naman silang impluwensya sa atin
Ipinapakita nito na may organisadong sistema na ng kalakalan at ugnayan ang mga Filipino
Ipinapakita nito na tayo ay mga watak-watak na grupo na walang ugnayan
Ipinapakita nito na ang mga Filipino noon ay nakadepende lamang sa ibang bansa
questions.rationale: Ang sistemang ito ay patunay na bago dumating ang mga Kastila, mayroon na tayong maunlad na ugnayang pang-ekonomiya at panlipunan.

questions.question: Kung susuriin ang sistemang 'Binatuan', bakit ito mas epektibo kaysa sa sistemang pagbabayad ng cash sa isang lipunang walang sentralisadong pamahalaan?
options: Dahil mas gusto ng mga sinaunang tao ang utang kaysa cash
Dahil pinapatibay nito ang pagkakaisa at pananagutan sa bawat miyembro ng komunidad
Dahil wala silang konsepto ng pera noon
Dahil mas madali itong subaybayan ng mga pinuno
questions.rationale: Sa kawalan ng pera, ang social capital (tiwala) ang nagsisilbing pera, kaya mas matibay ang pagkakaisa.

questions.question: Bakit mahalagang pag-aralan ang mga katutubong pamamaraan ng ugnayan gaya ng Ilaya at Ilawod sa pagbuo ng ating pambansang identidad?

Upang maunawaan ang ating kakayahan na magkaisa at makipagpalitan batay sa paggalang at tiwala
Upang gayahin ang mga sinaunang paraan at talikuran ang modernong teknolohiya
Upang malaman kung aling grupo ang mas nakakaangat noon
questions.rationale: Ang pag-unawa sa ating kasaysayan ay mahalaga upang makita ang mga ugat ng ating kultura ng pagtutulungan at bayanihan.

competencies.title: Nasusuri ang umiiral na paniniwala at pananampalataya ng kalinangang Pilipino
competencies.notes: Focus on Ginhawa, Manunggul Jar, and Anting-anting.

questions.question: Ano ang pangunahing kahulugan ng 'ginhawa' sa pananaw ng mga sinaunang Pilipino?
options: Kayamanan at materyal na ari-arian
Hininga o puwersa ng buhay
Kawalan ng anumang sakit sa katawan
Kaginhawaan sa buhay matapos ang pagtatrabaho
questions.rationale: Ang ginhawa sa sinaunang pananaw ay tumutukoy sa 'life force' o hininga ng tao.

questions.question: Alin sa mga sumusunod ang nagsisilbing simbolo ng tapang at proteksiyon sa mga sinaunang Pilipino?
options: Manunggul Jar
Kalasag
Anting-anting
Banga
questions.rationale: Ang anting-anting ay pinaniniwalaang nagbibigay ng proteksiyon laban sa masamang espiritu.

questions.question: Ano ang ipinahihiwatig ng paglalagay ng mga 'pabaon' sa libingan ng mga sinaunang Pilipino?
options: Bilang palamuti sa libingan ng yumao
Paraan ng pagpapakita ng yaman ng pamilya
Paniniwalang kailangan ito ng kaluluwa sa paglalakbay sa kabilang-buhay
Upang hindi na bumalik ang kaluluwa sa mundo ng mga buhay
questions.rationale: Ang pabaon ay bahagi ng ritwal na nagpapakita ng paniniwala sa pagpapatuloy ng buhay pagkatapos ng kamatayan.

questions.question: Bakit itinuturing na mahalagang ebidensya ang Manunggul Jar tungkol sa paniniwala ng mga sinaunang Pilipino?
options: Dahil ito ay yari sa ginto
Dahil ipinapakita nito ang paglalakbay ng kaluluwa patungo sa kabilang-buhay
Dahil ito ang pinakamatandang kagamitang panluto
Dahil ito ay ginagamit sa pakikipagkalakalan sa ibang bansa
questions.rationale: Ang disenyo ng Manunggul Jar, partikular ang bangka, ay sumisimbolo sa paglalakbay ng kaluluwa.

questions.question: Paano ipinapakita ng mga sinaunang Pilipino ang kanilang paggalang sa mga yumao?
options: Sa pamamagitan ng pag-aalay at pagpapanatili ng ugnayan sa mga anito
Sa pamamagitan ng paglimot sa nakaraan ng yumao
Sa pamamagitan ng pagtatapon ng gamit ng namatay
Sa pamamagitan ng pagpapatayo ng malalaking gusali
questions.rationale: Ang pag-aalay at paniniwala sa anito ay bahagi ng paggalang sa mga ninuno.

questions.question: Ang pagkakaroon ng anting-anting ay nagpapakita ng anong pagpapahalaga sa lipunang barangay?
options: Paghahangad na maging pinuno
Pagpapahalaga sa pisikal na kaligtasan at buhay
Pagkakaroon ng interes sa mga hiyas
Pagkakaroon ng tiwala sa ibang tao
questions.rationale: Ang anting-anting ay simbolo ng pag-iingat sa buhay na pinahahalagahan ng mga sinaunang Pilipino.

questions.question: Kung ang isang mandirigma ay may suot na anting-anting, paano ito makakaapekto sa kanyang kilos sa labanan?
options: Magiging maingat siya at hindi na lalaban
Magkakaroon siya ng lakas ng loob at kumpiyansa sa harap ng panganib
Aasa na lamang siya sa swerte at hindi na magsasanay
Iisipin niyang hindi siya maaaring sugatan kaya hindi na siya magtatago
questions.rationale: Ang paniniwala sa proteksiyon ng anting-anting ay nagbibigay ng sikolohikal na lakas sa tao.

questions.question: Paano mo uugnayin ang paniniwala sa kabilang-buhay sa araw-araw na pamumuhay ng mga sinaunang Pilipino?

Dahil sa paniniwalang ito, naging maingat sila sa paggawa ng mga ritwal at paggalang sa kalikasan
Dahil sa paniniwalang ito, tumigil sila sa pagsasaka
Dahil sa paniniwalang ito, wala silang pakialam sa ay kanilang mga ninuno
questions.rationale: Ang paniniwala sa kabilang-buhay ay nagdidikta ng disiplina at paggalang sa mga nakatatanda at kalikasan.

questions.question: Paano naiiba ang konsepto ng kamatayan ng mga sinaunang Pilipino sa modernong pananaw ngayon?
options: Ang mga sinaunang Pilipino ay walang takot sa kamatayan
Ang mga sinaunang Pilipino ay naniniwala sa pagpapatuloy ng ugnayan sa pagitan ng buhay at patay
Ang modernong pananaw ay mas nakatuon sa ritwal kaysa sa sinaunang panahon
Walang pagkakaiba ang dalawang pananaw
questions.rationale: Sinaunang pananaw: ugnayan ng buhay at patay; Moderno: mas nakatuon sa pisikal na pagtatapos.

questions.question: Ano ang implikasyon ng paggamit ng Manunggul Jar sa pag-unawa sa kalinangang Pilipino?
options: Ito ay patunay ng mataas na antas ng sining at pananampalataya
Ito ay nagpapakita na ang mga Pilipino ay mahilig sa banga
Ito ay nagpapakita ng kawalan ng koneksyon sa mga dayuhan
Ito ay simpleng gamit lamang at walang malalim na kahulugan
questions.rationale: Ang Manunggul Jar ay simbolo ng komplikadong pananaw ng mga ninuno sa buhay at kamatayan.

questions.question: Paano nasasalamin ng mga ritwal sa paglilibing ang pagpapahalaga ng lipunang barangay sa indibidwal?
options: Ipinapakita nito na ang tao ay walang halaga pagkatapos mamatay
Ipinapakita nito na mahalaga ang pagpapatuloy ng dignidad ng tao kahit siya ay pumanaw na
Ipinapakita nito na ang libing ay para lamang sa mga mahihirap
Ipinapakita nito na ang lipunan ay walang interes sa relihiyon
questions.rationale: Ang maayos na ritwal ay nagpapakita ng mataas na pagpapahalaga sa dignidad ng tao.

questions.question: Sa iyong pagsusuri, bakit itinuturing na mahalaga ang konsepto ng 'ginhawa' sa pagbuo ng katatagan ng mga sinaunang Pilipino?

Dahil ito ay ginagamit na pambayad sa buwis
Dahil ito ang nagtatakda kung sino ang magiging datu
Dahil ito ay para lamang sa mga taong walang sakit
questions.rationale: Ang paniniwalang ang tao ay may 'hininga' o 'ginhawa' mula sa mas mataas na puwersa ang nagbibigay ng tiwala sa sarili.

Ang mga ritwal ay nagsilbing tali na nagbubuklod sa mga tao sa kanilang paniniwala at tradisyon
Ang mga ritwal ay nagdudulot ng gulo sa barangay
Ang mga ritwal ay para lamang sa mga taong gustong magpakitang-gilas
questions.rationale: Ang mga ritwal ay nagpapatibay ng pagkakakilanlan at pagkakaisa ng mga miyembro ng lipunan.

options: Dahil kung ang buhay ay mahalaga, ang paglalakbay ng kaluluwa ay nararapat na bigyang-halaga rin
Dahil ang paghahanda sa libing ay mahalaga upang makatipid sa gastusin
Dahil ang mga sinaunang Pilipino ay takot mamatay
Dahil ang kamatayan ay itinuturing na pagtatapos ng lahat ng bagay
questions.rationale: Ang pagkilala sa halaga ng buhay ay umaabot hanggang sa kabilang-buhay sa kanilang pananaw.

Gitnang bahagi ng kapatagan

Mga kagamitang yari sa kahoy at dagta
Mga simbolo ng yaman tulad ng porselana, tanso, at gong

Kailangan nila ng mga gintong alahas para sa ritwal
Kailangan nila ng mga balangay para sa paglalakbay
Kailangan nila ng mga lupang matataba para sa pangingisda

Dito ginaganap ang mga seremonya ng kasal sa pagitan ng mga tribo
Ito ang pangunahing imbakan ng lahat ng bahandi
questions.rationale: Ang mga ilog ang nagsisilbing daluyan ng kalakal at lugar kung saan nagtatagpo (tabuan) ang mga grupo.

Dahil ang pagbawi ng tiwala ay may kaakibat na kahihiyan at parusa
Dahil mas madaling magpalit ng produkto kung magkaibigan
Dahil ito ang tanging paraan para maging pinuno
questions.rationale: Ang kredibilidad ay nakasalalay sa pagtupad sa pangako; ang paglabag ay nagdudulot ng kahihiyan.

Ang pagtatayo ng mga pabrika sa mga bundok
Ang pagbabawal sa kalakalan sa pagitan ng lungsod at kanayunan
Ang paggamit ng mga modernong sasakyan sa halip na ilog
questions.rationale: Ang pangangailangan ng bundok sa dagat (isda/asin) at kabundukan (gulay/kahoy) ay buhay na konsepto sa ating ekonomiya.
